newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH 1996 CAMPAIGN BEET SUGAR OUTPUT RISES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH 1996 CAMPAIGN BEET SUGAR OUTPUT RISES.

text.p: Czech beet sugar production from 1996 beet rose to 610,000 tonnes from 460,035 tonnes produced in the 1995 campaign, creating a surplus, the Agriculture Ministry said on Monday.
The ministry's plant production department head, Ivan Branzovsky, told Reuters that the surplus left for export is about 150,000 tonnes, up from the earlier forecasted 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
"Domestic consumption, including purchases for state reserves, will be about 460,000 tonnes...leaving 150,000 tonnes for exports," Branzovsky said.
The ministry said earlier that the state would buy some 20,000 tonnes for reserves.
The total area sown was 103,668 hectares, up from 94,334 hectares in 1995, while hectare yield of beet rose to 41.63 tonnes from 38.86 tonnes.
A total of 4.316 million tonnes of beet was harvested, after 3.666 million tonnes in 1995, and the yield of sugar from beet rose to 14.23 percent from 12.55 percent.
Czech sugar prices exceed those on the world market due to relatively liberal market conditions, and industry experts have said during the campaign that it would be difficult to export the surplus.
The Czech sugar market is protected by a 65 percent tariff.
The Czechs used to export some surplus sugar to Slovakia
under a no-tariff customs union agreement between the two
countries, but Slovakia's production last year of 226,000
tonnes will exceed domestic demand by some 20,000 tonnes.
Jiri Krousky, chairman of Czech sugar growers' association,
on Monday estimated that the Czech surplus would lead to a
decrease in the beet growing area this year to 95,000 to
100,000 hectares.
